title: fNIRSAtlas: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Classification
claim: A benchmark unifies heterogeneous datasets into one standardized pipeline that supports reproducible evaluation under both cross-subject and within-subject splits.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; task-suite boxes beside train/eval split diagram
description: The figure has two framed panels. The left panel has six rounded, pastel-colored boxes, one for each task suite: Motor, Mental Arithmetic, Motor Imagery, N-back, Emotion and MISC. Each box lists its epoch count, for example Motor with 8956. Under the boxes is a cartoon of a person wearing an fNIRS optode cap. The right panel is a flowchart. At the top, a row of subject boxes is split into training and evaluation groups for cross-subject classification. In the center, stacked fNIRS signal traces labelled Standardised Data Format feed through an arrow into a box reading Any ML Model, with PyTorch, BrainDecode, Aeon and SKLearn as examples. A second arrow leads to a box of predicted label percentages, with the top prediction in green and the others in red. At the bottom, epochs from one subject are split into training and evaluation groups for within-subject classification. The eye goes first to the colorful task boxes and the headset cartoon.
caption: Visual abstract of fNIRSAtlas. The benchmark integrates 23 classification tasks from 19 public data collections across multiple task suites into a standardized pipeline from raw recordings to benchmark tasks and model evaluation, enabling reproducible comparison of machine learning methods in both within-subject and cross-subject settings.
abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is a promising modality for brain-computer interfaces and cognitive state decoding, but progress in machine learning for fNIRS has been limited by small, isolated datasets and inconsistent evaluation protocols. We introduce fNIRSAtlas, the largest open benchmark for fNIRS classification to date, comprising 23 classification tasks from 19 public data collections, spanning diverse experimental paradigms, including motor execution, motor imagery, mental arithmetic, working memory, and emotion recognition. fNIRSAtlas provides a fully automated pipeline from raw data to evaluation and defines standardized benchmark tasks for both cross-subject and within-subject classification, ensuring reproducible comparison of methods. We evaluate a variety of baseline models from fNIRS and related neuroimaging and time-series machine learning literature on the benchmark. Our results demonstrate that performance varies substantially across tasks and that methods validated on limited data -- especially deep learning approaches -- often fail to generalize beyond their original evaluation. fNIRSAtlas serves as an extensible, open, and reproducible benchmark to support more robust and cumulative progress in machine learning for fNIRS data. Our code and data can be found at https://fnirsatlas.github.io.
